Option (a): N ÷ T X Q - C + B

N ÷ T means N is the husband of T

T X Q means T is the daughter-in-law of Q

Q - C means Q is the mother of C

C + B means C is the daughter of B

B is the father of N.

So, option (a) is correct.

Option (b): B - L - R ÷ D + N

B - L means B is the mother of L

L - R means L is the mother of R

R ÷ D means R is the husband of D

D + N means D is the daughter of N

B is the mother of N's daughter's mother-in-law.

So, option (b) is incorrect.

Option (c): N X Q ÷ V + S - B

N X Q means N is the daughter-in-law of Q

Q ÷ V means Q is the husband of V

V + S means V is the daughter of S

S - B means S is the mother of B

B is the sibling of N's mother-in-law.

So, option (c) is incorrect.

Option (d): B ÷ D - J ÷ R + N

B ÷ D means B is the husband of D

D - J means D is the mother of J

J ÷ R means J is the husband of R

R + N means R is the daughter of N

B is the father-in-law of N's daughter.

So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['be'] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): Sarah will thoroughly prepare the presentation on sustainable development.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate article(s) to fill in the blanks. For ___ past few decades, ___ number of people on Earth has been increasing.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate article(s) to fill in the blanks.

For ___ past few decades, ___ number of people on Earth has been increasing.
questions.solution:
The definite article "the" should be used in the first blank because the phrase refers to a specific time period ("past few decades") that is clearly understood from the context. We use "the" before phrases like "past few decades," "last year," or "next century" when referring to a known or specific time. Also, the specific time period given in the sentence is plural in nature. So, "a" and "an" would not be appropriate.

"____ number of people" is followed by the singular verb "has". The phrase, 'a number of' takes a plural noun and plural verb after it. The phrase, 'the number of' takes a plural noun but a singular verb after it. Since the phrase in the given sentence has the singular verb "has" after it, we would fill the second blank with "the".

The correct sentence is: For the past few decades, the number of people on Earth has been increasing.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun or plural noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun or singular noun.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) Genoa, Italy, a poor man named Peter; (b) making wool ready for the spinners (c) he earned his living by (d) many years ago there lived in
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) Genoa, Italy, a poor man named Peter;

(b) making wool ready for the spinners

(c) he earned his living by

(d) many years ago there lived in
questions.solution:
'd' is the introductory part that talks about an incident of the past, where the person lived is mentioned in 'a'. Parts 'c' and 'b' form a mandatory pair as 'c' starts the discussion about the person's way of earning and 'b' describes his means of earning.

The correct sequence of the parts of the sentence is d,a,c,b.

The sentence is - "Many years ago there lived in Genoa, Italy, a poor man named Peter; he earned his living by making wool ready for the spinners."

Hence, option (c) is correct.

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb [being] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "Cake and muffins were being baked by me for my nephew's birthday last week."

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Because nanoparticles are so tiny, they can easily get into plants and help they grow .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Because nanoparticles are so tiny, they can easily get into plants and help they grow.
questions.solution:
The given sentence uses "they" instead of "them," which is grammatically wrong. The object of the verb "help" should be in the objective case ("them"), not the subjective case ("they").

The correct sentence is: Because nanoparticles are so tiny, they can easily get into plants and help them grow.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Option (b): "Helps" is a singular verb, but the subject "nanoparticles" is plural, so "help" [plural verb] should be used instead. Also, the pronoun "they" is incorrect here; it should be "them" because it is the object of the verb "help."

Option (c): This is incorrect because "helped" changes the tense to past, while the sentence is written in the present tense. There is no indication in the context that a past tense is required.

Note: Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The company have/ been expanding/ its operations globally/ for the past year.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The company have/ been expanding/ its operations globally/ for the past year.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'the company have'.

The error is related to subject-verb agreement.

"Company" is a singular noun, so it should be followed by the singular verb "has," not the plural verb "have."

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The company has been expanding its operations globally for the past year.

Note:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.solution:

The error lies in the lack of an article before the noun "mystery."

When we refer to a specific, singular noun like "mystery," we use the definite article to specify it.

The context refers to a specific mystery that the detective was trying to solve. The correct article to use in this context is the definite article "the." Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The detective was trying to solve the mystery behind the stolen painting.

NOTE:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
